Question in plain words: One deposit shows two different numbers. Which is right: DEP-4841 or DEP2-4841?
What happens today (one example): Deposit of $200.00 (Cash) on work order S2-40392 for ZZAUTOTEST RGWO Customer A: Customer > Deposits tab shows No. DEP-4841; Customer > Payments tab, the $0.00 payment opened, shows the same deposit as DEP2-4841.
Sources found and why they do not settle: Confluence 263094273 "Deposits for Work Orders" (last modified 16 Apr 2026) SV-5675 says "The deposit will get a CP- unique number same to a credit (e.g. CP3-1234)" - the prefix is no longer CP and it does not say which screens show the location part. SV-10762 (Done, Oct 2026) asked to "make every deposit surface consistent" but is about the memo, not the deposit number.
My recommendation: Fix it: show the same number on both tabs, with the location part (DEP2-4841), like work order and invoice numbers (S2-40392).

Area: Work Order lifecycle
Question in plain words: If a technician is still clocked in when the last line is completed with the Complete button, should the work order become Complete (Require Review is Off)?
What happens today (one example): S2-40397 (and S2-40391): Admin clocked in on the line; line completed with Complete; work order stayed In Progress. After the clock-out it went to Review, not Complete, although Require Review Before Completion is Off.
Sources found and why they do not settle: Confluence 646021121 "Simple Mode - Streamlined Work Order Completion & Bulk Receiving" (last modified 16 Jul 2026) Story 16 R12: "When the WO's last remaining open line becomes resolved ... OFF -> the WO is auto-marked Complete ... regardless of how the last line resolves"; R13: "A clock-out that finishes the last line routes the WO to Ready for Review even when review is OFF". Here the clock-out did not finish the line - the Complete button did - so neither sentence covers it. Confluence 771391574 "Simple Flow V2" (epic SV-8683, last modified 11 Sep 2026) Story 9: "A work order becomes complete because its lines are".
My recommendation: Fix it: follow R12 - Complete as soon as the last line is completed with the Complete button, even if someone is still clocked in.
Notes: Draft: C2-*/TICKET.html and CHRIS-COMMENT.html. Not filed; nothing posted.

Area: Work Order lifecycle
Question in plain words: With Require Tech Story Off, should clocking out with "Line Completed?" switched on still demand a tech story?
What happens today (one example): S2-40396: Admin clocked in on line "ZZ A1 repro line", opened Clock Out, switched Line Completed? on, left the story empty, pressed Clock Out: "Tech story is a required field" and no clock-out (same on S2-40391).
Sources found and why they do not settle: Confluence 771391574 "Simple Flow V2" (epic SV-8683, last modified 11 Sep 2026) Story 5 (SV-9251): "The other line-level requirements stay: tech story, mileage, engine hours, each only when its setting is on" and the list of entry points includes "clock out"; but the same page also says "At clock out we will open current prod modal, when technician needs to toggle the Line completed" and "If a tech story is required and empty, it is required at clock out" - it does not say whether "required" here means the setting.
My recommendation: Fix it: follow the setting - when Require Tech Story is Off, Clock Out with Line Completed? on should not demand a story.
